public.theorem_title: A fifth-power estimate transfers an asymptotic exponent
public.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.ArithmeticStageBounds.powerBound_of_fifth : ∀ {f g : Nat → Nat} {a : Real} (hg : ThreeSum.StageBounds.PowerBound g a)
  (hfg :
    ∀ (n : Nat),
      @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
        (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
          (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid))) (f n)
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 5) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 5))))
        (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 256) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 256)))
          (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
            (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid))) (g n)
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 8) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 8)))))),
  ThreeSum.StageBounds.PowerBound f
    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Real Real Real (@instHMul.{0} Real Real.instMul)
      (@HDiv.hDiv.{0, 0, 0} Real Real Real (@instHDiv.{0} Real (@DivInvMonoid.toDiv.{0} Real Real.instDivInvMonoid))
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Real (nat_lit 8)
          (@instOfNatAtLeastTwo.{0} Real (nat_lit 8) Real.instNatCast
            (@Nat.instAtLeastTwoHAddOfNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 7) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 7)))
              (@Nat.instNeZeroSucc (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 6) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 6)))))))
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Real (nat_lit 5)
          (@instOfNatAtLeastTwo.{0} Real (nat_lit 5) Real.instNatCast
            (@Nat.instAtLeastTwoHAddOfNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 4) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 4)))
              (@Nat.instNeZeroSucc (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 3) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 3))))))))
      a) := by
  sorry
public.natural_language_statement:
Let $f,g:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and $a\in\mathbb R$. Say a function has power bound $a$ when, for every $\varepsilon>0$, it is eventually at most $n^{a+\varepsilon}$. Suppose $g$ has power bound $a$ and $f(n)^5\le256g(n)^8$ for every $n$. Then

$$\forall\varepsilon>0,\quad f(n)\le n^{(8/5)a+\varepsilon}\quad\text{for all sufficiently large }n.$$

This converts an exact integer estimate for a rounded arithmetic cost into the real exponent bound used in the runtime ledger.

public.theorem_title: Stored wanted-pair slots have distinct index pairs
public.natural_language_statement:
Let $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ satisfy the wanted-pair output specification at base $f$, for left and right integer arrays of lengths $N_L,N_R$, modulus $M\in\mathbb N$, and shift $s\in\mathbb Z$. This specification stores without repetition the index pairs $(i,j)$ with $i<N_L$, $j<N_R$, and $M\mid\mathrm{left}(i)+s-\mathrm{right}(j)$. Let $L(k),R(k)$ be the two indices read from stored slot $k$. For valid slots $k,k'<(\mu(f))_{\mathbb N}$,

$$
L(k)=L(k')\ \land\ R(k)=R(k')\quad\Longrightarrow\quad k=k'.
$$

Here the subscript denotes integer-to-natural conversion. The result supplies distinct labels for the dense guard even when input values or residue keys repeat.

public.theorem_title: Band representation survives preservation of the memory prefix
public.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.LightBandPreprocessing.Represents.keep : ∀ {μ μ' : Nat → Int} {values endpoints g bound : Nat}
  {hg : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))) g}
  {original L : List.{0} Int} {hs : @List.Pairwise.{0} Int (fun (x1 x2 : Int) => @LT.lt.{0} Int Int.instLTInt x1 x2) L}
  (h : ThreeSum.LightBandPreprocessing.Represents μ values endpoints g hg original L hs) (hk : Light.Kept μ μ' bound)
  (hv :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) values (@List.length.{0} Int original)) bound)
  (he :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) endpoints
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))))
        (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))) (@List.length.{0} Int original)))
      bound),
  ThreeSum.LightBandPreprocessing.Represents μ' values endpoints g hg original L hs := by
  sorry
public.natural_language_statement:
Let $O,L$ be integer lists with $L$ strictly increasing, let $g>0$ be a natural band size, and let $v,e,b\in\mathbb N$ be addresses and a cutoff. Write $\mathcal R_\mu(v,e,g;O,L)$ for the representation that stores $L$ at $v$, has $|L|\le|O|$ and the same value membership as $O$, and stores its length, band count, and lower/upper endpoints at the header $e$. Suppose integer memories $\mu,\mu'$ agree at every address below $b$, and
$v+|O|\le b$ and $e+2+2|O|\le b$. Then

$$
\mathcal R_\mu(v,e,g;O,L)\Longrightarrow
\mathcal R_{\mu'}(v,e,g;O,L).
$$

The result allows later computation beyond the cutoff to preserve the normalized class and its band data as one reusable invariant.

public.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.LightBandRawAColor.tables_keep : ∀ {μ ν : Nat → Int} {tables bound : Nat} {A B C : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Family}
  (ht : ThreeSum.LightBandEnumeration.Tables μ tables A B C) (hk : Light.Kept μ ν bound)
  (hb :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) tables
        (ThreeSum.LightBandEnumeration.count A.size B.size C.size))
      bound),
  ThreeSum.LightBandEnumeration.Tables ν tables A B C := by

public.natural_language_statement:
Let $A,B,C$ be finite families of nonempty, sorted, pairwise separated integer intervals, with sizes $n_A,n_B,n_C$. Their three consecutive owner tables store interval-lookup results for the $B\times C$, $A\times B$, and $A\times C$ pairs. Let $\mathcal T_\mu(t;A,B,C)$ denote that table representation in integer memory $\mu$, starting at address $t$.

Suppose memories $\mu,\nu$ agree below a natural cutoff $b$ and $t+n_Bn_C+n_An_B+n_An_C\le b$. Then

$$
\mathcal T_\mu(t;A,B,C)\Longrightarrow
\mathcal T_\nu(t;A,B,C).
$$

This preserves the owner-table invariant while later catalog construction writes in higher memory, without imposing any further condition on the interval values.

public.theorem_title: Prepared sorted bands depend only on their allocated regions
public.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.LightSortedBands.Prepared.transfer : ∀ {μ μ' : Nat → Int} {values endpoints g : Nat} {original : List.{0} Int}
  (h : ThreeSum.LightSortedBands.Prepared μ values endpoints g original)
  (hk :
    ∀ (a : Nat),
      Or
          (And (@LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat values a)
            (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat a
              (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) values (@List.length.{0} Int original))))
          (And (@LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat endpoints a)
            (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat a
              (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
                (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) endpoints
                  (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))))
                (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
                  (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))) (@List.length.{0} Int original))))) →
        @Eq.{1} Int (μ' a) (μ a)),
  ThreeSum.LightSortedBands.Prepared μ' values endpoints g original := by
  sorry
public.natural_language_statement:
Let $O$ be an integer list, let $v,e,g\in\mathbb N$, and let $\mu,\mu'$ be integer memories. The predicate $\mathcal P_\mu(v,e,g;O)$ means that some strictly increasing list of the same values as $O$, of length at most $|O|$, is stored at $v$, with the prescribed length and band-count headers and lower/upper endpoints at $e$. Suppose the memories agree throughout
$[v,v+|O|)$ and $[e,e+2+2|O|)$. Then

$$
\mathcal P_\mu(v,e,g;O)\Longrightarrow
\mathcal P_{\mu'}(v,e,g;O).
$$

The band-size parameter $g$ is any natural number.

This specifies exactly which regions must be retained when later machine stages modify other parts of memory.

public.theorem_title: A uniform two-parameter polynomial bound from an eventual power bound
public.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.PolynomialResources.pair_polyBound_of_powerBound : ∀ {f : Nat → Nat} {a : Real} (hf : ThreeSum.StageBounds.PowerBound f a) (e : Nat),
  ∃ (s : Nat) (k : Nat),
    ∀ (n U : Nat),
      @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
        (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) (f n)
          (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
            (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid)))
            (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) U
              (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
            e))
        (Light.polyBound s k (@List.cons.{0} Nat n (@List.cons.{0} Nat U (@List.nil.{0} Nat)))) := by
  sorry
public.natural_language_statement:
Let $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, let $a\in\mathbb R$, and suppose that for every $\varepsilon>0$, one has $f(n)\le n^{a+\varepsilon}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. For every fixed $e\in\mathbb N$, there exist $s,k\in\mathbb N$ such that

$$
\forall n,U\in\mathbb N,\qquad
f(n)(U+1)^e\le 2^s\bigl((n+1)(U+1)\bigr)^k.
$$

The expression on the right is the compiler's polynomial resource bound for the two parameters $n$ and $U$. Its constants are independent of both parameters, and the inequality holds at every input size, including the finitely many sizes excluded by the eventual hypothesis.

This converts asymptotic resource envelopes into the uniform polynomial limits required for compilation.

public.theorem_title: Adding two costs preserves their common power bound
public.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.StageBounds.PowerBound.add_same : ∀ {f g : Nat → Nat} {a : Real} (hf : ThreeSum.StageBounds.PowerBound f a) (hg : ThreeSum.StageBounds.PowerBound g a),
  ThreeSum.StageBounds.PowerBound
    (fun (n : Nat) => @HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) (f n) (g n)) a := by
  sorry
public.natural_language_statement:
Let $f,g:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and $a\in\mathbb R$. Suppose each function has power bound $a$: for every positive slack, each is eventually bounded by $n$ raised to $a$ plus that slack. Then their sum has the same power bound:

$$\forall\varepsilon>0,\quad f(n)+g(n)\le n^{a+\varepsilon}\quad\text{for all sufficiently large }n.$$

This closure property combines separate stage costs without increasing their common asymptotic exponent.

public.theorem_title: Splitting the head of a stored memory segment
public.formal_statement:
theorem Light.seg_cons : ∀ {μ : Nat → Int} {a : Nat} {l : List.{0} Int} {x : Int},
  Iff (Light.Seg μ a (@List.cons.{0} Int x l))
    (And (@Eq.{1} Int (μ a) x)
      (Light.Seg μ
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) a
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
        l)) := by
  sorry
public.natural_language_statement:
Let $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ be memory, $a$ a starting address, $x\in\mathbb Z$, and $L$ a list of integers. Write $\operatorname{Seg}(\mu,a,L)$ when memory at addresses $a+i$ contains $L_i$ for every $i<|L|$. Then

$$\operatorname{Seg}(\mu,a,x::L)\iff\mu(a)=x\;\land\;\operatorname{Seg}(\mu,a+1,L).$$

This gives the head-and-tail rule for reading or constructing contiguous memory representations.

public.theorem_title: Concatenation corresponds to adjacent memory segments
public.formal_statement:
theorem Light.seg_append : ∀ {μ : Nat → Int} {a : Nat} {l₁ l₂ : List.{0} Int},
  Iff
    (Light.Seg μ a
      (@HAppend.hAppend.{0, 0, 0} (List.{0} Int) (List.{0} Int) (List.{0} Int)
        (@instHAppendOfAppend.{0} (List.{0} Int) (@List.instAppend.{0} Int)) l₁ l₂))
    (And (Light.Seg μ a l₁)
      (Light.Seg μ (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) a (@List.length.{0} Int l₁)) l₂)) := by
  sorry
public.natural_language_statement:
Let $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ be memory, $a\in\mathbb N$ an address, and $L_1,L_2$ lists of integers. The predicate $\operatorname{Seg}(\mu,a,L)$ means that memory contains $L$ consecutively from address $a$. Then

$$\operatorname{Seg}(\mu,a,L_1\mathbin{+\!+}L_2)\iff\operatorname{Seg}(\mu,a,L_1)\land\operatorname{Seg}(\mu,a+|L_1|,L_2).$$

This equivalence allows a contiguous array representation to be split at a list boundary or assembled from adjacent pieces, including empty pieces.
